items.title: Suspected serial offender linked to IS walks free over filmed gay bashing
items.description: A suspected serial violent homophobe linked to an Islamic State terrorist network has walked free on probation after pleading guilty to a brutal snuff-video-style gay bashing.

items.title: US tariffs on Australia remain at 10 per cent — for now
items.description: Trade Minister Don Farrell hopes Australia can dodge a higher tariff rate being imposed by the US, saying trade officials overnight confirmed the tariff rate on Australia would remain at 10 per cent — at least for now.

items.title: PM apologises if Grace Tame 'difficult' label misinterpreted
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has offered a qualified apology for calling 2021 Australian of the Year and child sexual abuse survivor Grace Tame "difficult", saying he was referring to her "difficult life".

items.title: How much compromise is too much? Labor's capital gains conundrum
items.description: The hints are getting less subtle and Labor's plans on capital gains tax are becoming clearer, but a proposal laden with compromises risks undermining any intergenerational argument.

items.title: Man accused of Sydney grandfather's killing 'no mastermind', lawyer says
items.description: Two men are charged over the alleged kidnapping and death of Sydney grandfather Chris Baghsarian.

items.title: Breaking: Teen confirmed as first Australian death from tick-induced red meat allergy
items.description: Jeremy Webb's death in 2022 is the first documented fatal case of mammalian meat allergy in the country and second in the world.

items.title: Australians urged to consider leaving Israel and Lebanon
items.description: The Australian government is urging Australians to consider leaving Israel and Lebanon, as the prospect of US strikes on Iran puts the region on high alert.

items.title: Live: National alert test to trigger siren on mobile phones in July
items.description: Trials for a new national alerts messaging system will begin this year, the federal emergency management minister says. Follow live.

items.title: Albanese bomb threat is latest flashpoint in a risk already 'flashing red'
items.description: Spitting, assault and online abuse are rising signs of a dangerous political culture in Australia.

items.title: RBA governor says she does not think inflation is taking off again
items.description: Michelle Bullock gives more details on how quickly developments affecting monetary policy have moved since the middle of last year.

items.title: Live: ASX opens higher, Qantas slips on flat profit, Optus accused of 'lack of care' culture
items.description: The ASX has joined the global risk-on rally, gaining ground on opening, while Qantas is down after posting a flat first-half result. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Mother's fight for Deafblind child to access local school makes history
items.description: Australia's first Deafblind class in a mainstream school has been established after a mother spent two years advocating for her son.

items.title: 'Nothing is going to happen': Female athletes speak out on gender-based violence
items.description: Experiences shared by athletes who participated in the ABC's Elite Athletes in Australian Women's Sport survey found many fear "nothing is going to happen" when speaking out on gender-based violence and harassment.

items.title: Cuba kills four aboard US-registered speedboat who opened fire on guards
items.description: Cuban forces killed four people and wounded six others aboard a Florida-based speedboat that entered Cuban waters and opened fire on a Cuban patrol, the country's government says.

items.title: INXS nominated for induction into Rock & Roll Hall of Fame
items.description: INXS will be considered for induction into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and is one of 10 first-time nominees on the ballot.

items.title: From the first Mardi Gras to RuPaul, do you know your queer history?
items.description: Australia's LGBTQIA+ history is full to the brim with groundbreaking art, brave protests and lots of fun along the way. Test how much you know about the queer trailblazers of our country in this quiz.

items.title: Preaching kindness, Amanda Seyfried went all in on her latest role
items.description: The Oscar-nominated star adored working with director Mona Fastvold to resurrect an astonishing religious figure in The Testament of Ann Lee.

items.title: How shed boxes became one of the most precious collections in Australia
items.description: The ABC gets a rare look at the Aboriginal History Archive, a little-known collection of thousands of items collected by the well-known activist Gary Foley.

items.title: Potential for major drought relief as tropical low heads south
items.description: The tropical low currently flooding outback Australia is tipped to track south this weekend, reaching south-east states early next week.

items.title: Bill Gates speaks 'candidly' to staff about relationship with Epstein
items.description: Bill Gates addresses his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein in a staff meeting after increased scrutiny over photos and emails in the Epstein files.

items.title: The 'common' AI-related crimes Australians fear most
items.description: More than half of Australian adults are worried about AI being used to cause them harm, and almost as many fear falling victim to a crime enabled by the technology, a report found.

items.title: Suffered inappropriate treatment for endometriosis? Here's what to do
items.description: If allegations that a surgeon undertook surgery for "severe" endometriosis in women with little or no sign of the disease have you questioning your own treatment, here is where you can voice your concerns.

items.title: Super industry sounds alarm about increased switching to 'riskier' funds
items.description: More young Australians with less super are moving away from tightly regulated super funds to platform-based or self-managed super funds.

items.title: Pre-dawn carjacking at Chinese takeaway prompts staff to leave regional town
items.description: A Top End Chinese restaurant manager says the eatery's staff have left town after its chef was allegedly threatened with a knife in a pre-dawn carjacking.

items.title: First there was K-pop, now there's K-ball
items.description: Australia emerges as an unlikely getaway for some of South Korea's biggest baseball stars.
